best_for: Developers on Linux or Windows who resolve merge conflicts and compare folders often, and want a free visual tool that plugs into Git.

points.title: Two-way and three-way
points.text: Meld compares two or three files, or two or three folders, side by side. The three-way view helps you settle merge conflicts by showing both sides and the common base at once.

points.title: Works with your version control
points.text: It understands Git, Mercurial, Bazaar and Subversion, so you can review changes in a working copy before you commit.

points.title: Folder compare for syncing
points.text: Folder comparison flags missing and changed files and lets you ignore files or folders by pattern, which is handy for checking a backup or a deploy.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: Meld is free and open source under GPLv2 or later, with no paid edition.

points.title: Windows: no auto-update
points.text: The Windows installer works per user or for all users on x64, but the project says Meld does not yet update itself or offer a portable install. Check back for new versions yourself; the Windows listing keeps 6 of them.

points.title: macOS is not official and lags
points.text: The project says macOS is not yet supported. The Mac build here comes from a semi-official GitLab project and is on 3.22.3+105 while Windows and Linux are on 3.24.1. Homebrew and MacPorts are other routes.

points.title: Linux is home
points.text: Meld is packaged by most Linux distributions. The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and Arm64, is on Flathub but not marked verified there. Linux lists only the current release.
